$comment: The ONE fixture of the output normalization (DESIGN-conformance-suite.md §5, §9): a compiled program's stdout and
its expected output are compared after the host's newline (CR LF, or LF) becomes LF, each line loses its trailing
spaces (spaces only) and trailing line ends are dropped. Every other character is what the program printed and
stays: a lone CR, a form feed, NEL, LS and PS are not line ends, so a program that printed one where the expected
output holds a line end differs (kb/Work PB5460; .NET's String.ReplaceLineEndings, which the rule used to follow,
reads all of them as line ends). The rule exists in two languages by nature, run.py's normalize() and
holds BOTH to every case below, so the two runners of the suite compare outputs on one basis.

cases.name: lf, with a final line end
a lone cr is not a line end
cr then cr lf is a cr and one line end
nel, ls, ps and ff are not line ends
a form feed is not a line end
a vertical tab does not end a line
trailing spaces of each line go
a last line of spaces goes
an inner line of spaces becomes empty and stays
